title: Medical care in Zhangjiajie
text: First-aid stations are at every major cable car, elevator and bus stop - they can treat wounds and call stretchers (500-2,000 yuan). Wulingyuan People's Hospital is nearest the park, Zhangjiajie People's Hospital in the city has an international department and rabies vaccines.

title: Monkeys in the park - rules of engagement
text: Rhesus macaques live throughout Zhangjiajie, especially along Golden Whip Stream. Never show food, do not smile (bared teeth signal aggression), avoid direct eye contact, never touch babies. If a monkey grabs your bag, let go - things are not worth a bite.

title: Safety in Zhangjiajie
text: Zhangjiajie is one of the safest tourist destinations in the world - serious crime is virtually nonexistent. Watch for free tea ceremony scams, meterless taxis and pushy guides at park gates. The real dangers in the park are wet steps, aggressive monkeys and steep cliffs.

title: Language barrier in Zhangjiajie - mini phrasebook
text: Few people speak English in Zhangjiajie, even in hotels. Install offline Chinese packs in Google Translate before arrival. Key phrases: Ni hao (hello), Xie xie (thanks), Duo shao qian (how much), Bu yao la (not spicy), Ce suo zai na li (where is the toilet).

title: Internet and SIM cards in Zhangjiajie
text: A Chinese SIM from China Mobile or China Unicom at the airport is the best option - about 100 yuan for 10-20 GB over 30 days. eSIMs like Airalo work too. Install a VPN before arrival - Google, YouTube, Instagram and WhatsApp are all blocked in China.
